title: Latency-Aware Selective Verification in Generate–Validate NetOps Pipelines: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt-5-mini
abstract: We evaluate whether a selective, low-latency verification tier (risk scoring + fast validator) inserted into a generate–validate–repair pipeline reduces unsafe commits from LLM-generated network changes while meeting an operational latency SLO. We preregistered a paired confirmatory design (CAND-2026-001) and executed it end-to-end with gpt-5-mini and a deterministic NetOps validator. On 400 preregistered synthetic operator intents (10% adversarial/OOD), baseline (LLM-only) produced 399/400 valid proposals; guarded (selective verifier) produced 400/400 valid proposals. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025 (0.25 percentage points); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The execution manifest and scoring traces (paths and SHA-256 hashes) are archived. The observed absolute safety gain in this in-distribution synthetic corpus is small; preregistered latency SLO evaluation (H2) could not be completed from the provided confirmatory artifacts because latency telemetry for the pipelines is not present in the confirmatory outputs and is therefore unresolved. We release full artifact hashes and representative validator traces to enable reproducibility and stress the need for adversarial and multi-model follow-ups before operational deployment.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation and change activation is a core operator aim. LLM-driven NetOps workflows can accelerate NetOps but introduce risk: fluent but unsafe proposals can cause outages. Recent work augments LLMs with verifiers, digital twins, or iterative repair loops to improve safety. However, operators must trade verification latency against safety; a lightweight selective-verifier (risk scoring + fast validator) that only checks high-risk proposals could reduce unsafe commits while meeting latency SLOs. We preregistered CAND-2026-001 to evaluate whether such a selective verification tier (the "guarded" pipeline) yields a lower unsafe-commit rate than LLM-only (the "baseline") and whether it meets an end-to-end latency SLO. Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment with complete archived artifacts; (2) deterministic, artifact-backed primary analysis (400 paired items) reporting exact counts, test statistics, and bootstrap CIs; (3) transparent reconciliation and a candid account of unresolved latency telemetry and external-validity limitations.
sections.related_work: LLM-based NetOps and agentic repair systems increasingly combine generation with formal or simulator-based validation. Recent benchmarks examine LLM-driven configuration repair and agentic architectures that iterate with verification tools; other work integrates LLM agents with digital twins for validation. Our study differs: we test a latency-aware, selective verification intervention under a preregistered paired design and publish full execution and scoring artifacts. Representative nearest works (verified during the autonomous literature phase) include recent configuration-repair and verifier-augmented agent studies that motivated our selective-verifier architecture (see cited_record_ids).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and primary question: CAND-2026-001 (frozen before execution) defined the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and two confirmatory hypotheses: H1 (safety) and H2 (latency SLO). Key preregistered elements are archived (study id, analysis scripts, and preregistration SHA-256). Dataset and tasks: a deterministic synthetic intent generator produced 400 confirmatory intents spanning realistic NetOps change classes (ACLs, interface edits, route edits); 10% deterministic adversarial/OOD variants were included per the preregistration. Model and pipeline: all LLM generations used gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version in execution/model_configuration.json). Design choice (preregistered): independent_condition_generation = false (shared-initial candidate produced once per intent and reused across conditions), initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1 — this reduces generation variance between arms and isolates the verifier intervention; the design and its consequences were preregistered and are documented in the execution manifest. Validator and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 acted as the full-checker ground truth and scorer (scoring_rule full_intent_constraint_validation). Execution accounting (artifact-backed): planned episodes 800 (400 pairs), completed episodes 800, model_calls_used = 401 (execution manifest). Per the provider-call audit in the manifest, stage_counts record 400 shared_initial_generation events and 1 repair invocation (repair stage). The guarded pipeline therefore invoked only one additional model/repair call in this run (artifact-backed); no other repair/model-call activity was observed in the archived call audit. Analysis: primary analysis used the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor. We computed paired contingency counts, exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the estimand (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). All raw outputs, per-task scorer JSON, validator traces, and provider-call logs were archived and hash-summed (execution manifest artifact_hashes).
sections.results: Execution summary (artifact-backed): 400 complete pairs, 0 unrecovered infrastructure failures. Per-condition scoring (deterministic validator): baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975); guarded valid proposals = 400/400 (1.000). Paired contingency: n11 = 399, n10 = 1 (guarded success & baseline failure), n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Primary estimand (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% CI for difference = [0.0, 0.0075]. The single discordant case is archived (example episode present in execution/scoring and execution/responses; artifacts and hashes provided). Operational accounting note (artifact-backed): model_calls_used = 401; provider_call_audit stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 400, repair: 1}; condition_counts = {shared: 400, guarded: 1}. This reflects the preregistered shared-initial design and a single observed repair invocation in the guarded arm. Latency SLO (H2) status: preregistered H2 required 95th-percentile end-to-end latency ≤ 2000 ms and a latency comparison versus a full-checker baseline. The confirmatory artifact set does not include pipeline latency telemetry or completed latency secondary-results; therefore H2 cannot be evaluated from the provided confirmatory artifacts and remains unresolved in this report (explicit preregistration and execution manifest references are provided).
sections.discussion: Interpretation: In this synthetic, in-distribution corpus the baseline LLM proposals were already highly correct per the deterministic validator; the guarded pipeline produced one additional valid outcome out of 400 paired items. The observed absolute gain (0.25 percentage points) is small and not statistically distinguishable from zero in this dataset (discordance pattern n10=1, n01=0 yielded McNemar p=1.0 and bootstrap CI including zero). Operational implications: where baseline LLM correctness is near ceiling and validator semantics match task generation, a lightweight selective verifier may yield limited marginal safety gains; its value increases when baseline correctness is lower or under adversarial/OOD distributions. Design-note and reproducibility: the shared-initial candidate design (independent_condition_generation=false) was preregistered; it reduces generation variance and focuses the test on the verifier/repair intervention. The execution manifest and per-episode scorer/validator JSONs (paths and SHA-256 hashes) are provided so readers can audit the single discordant episode and overall accounting. Limitations (artifact-backed): (1) synthetic task corpus — not production traffic; (2) single model (gpt-5-mini) and single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); (3) shared-initial design reduces scope of inference to verifier effects given a single generated candidate per intent; (4) latency SLO (H2) cannot be assessed from confirmatory artifacts because latency telemetry is absent from the archived confirmatory outputs; (5) small absolute number of discordant cases limits statistical power to detect small improvements versus near-ceiling baselines. Recommendations: (i) evaluate selective verification across multiple LLMs and real-device digital twins; (ii) include full latency telemetry and end-to-end timing in future confirmatory artifacts to test operational SLOs; (iii) perform threshold sweeps on the risk-classifier on adversarial distributions to map verification-budget vs safety Pareto frontiers.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that compared a selective low-latency verifier intervention against LLM-only for intent→configuration proposals from gpt-5-mini. Artifact-backed primary analysis (400 paired intents) found baseline = 399/400 valid, guarded = 400/400 valid, paired difference = 0.0025 (95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0075], exact McNemar p = 1.0). The guarded pipeline produced one additional valid outcome; the absolute safety gain is small in this corpus. The run is fully archived: model responses, scorer JSON, validator traces, provider-call logs, and deterministic reconciliation checks with SHA-256 hashes. Critical operational questions remain: the latency SLO (H2) could not be evaluated from the confirmatory artifact set because pipeline latency telemetry is not present; we therefore do not claim to have met any latency SLO. The artifact bundle enables reproduction and extension; follow-on work should stress adversarial/OOD distributions, multiple models, and end-to-end latency measurement before operational adoption.

disclosure_statement: Mandatory Disclosure Statement: This study was an autonomous, post-lock research run under the frozen master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial prompt prior to autonomy lock; all subsequent literature review, design selection, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation were performed autonomously after the lock. Preregistration: CAND-2026-001 (preregistration SHA-256: 086d248e89636e99e788232e78a99b63459648545e6e79ed763c29521f8f8572) froze hypotheses, primary/secondary estimands, sampling plan, analysis scripts, and retry/missingness policies. Declared model and orchestration: LLM used = gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version per execution/model_configuration.json), provider adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1, execution_mode = scientific_confirmatory. Validator and scorer: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 acted as the full-checker ground truth and scorer (scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation). Key frozen design choices (recorded in preregistration and execution contract): independent_condition_generation = false (shared initial candidate per intent reused across conditions), initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, planned episodes = 800 (400 intents × 2 conditions), planned_model_calls = 800, planned retries and missingness rules as documented in the preregistration. Execution accounting (artifact-backed): completed episodes = 800, complete pairs = 400, model_calls_used = 401. Provider-call audit (deterministic reconciliation in execution manifest) records stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 400, "repair": 1} and condition_counts = {"shared": 400, "guarded": 1}; these archived counts reconcile observed provider calls and show the guarded pipeline triggered a single additional repair/model call in this run (artifact paths and SHA-256 hashes recorded in the execution manifest). All raw outputs, per-episode scorer JSON, validator traces, and provider-call logs were preserved and their SHA-256 hashes are listed in the execution manifest artifact_hashes. No human manually edited or rewrote the manuscript body after the autonomy lock. Deviations and unresolved items: preregistered H2 required end-to-end latency SLO evaluation (95th-percentile ≤ 2000 ms) and latency comparisons versus a full-checker baseline; the confirmatory artifact set does not include pipeline latency telemetry or completed secondary latency results, so H2 could not be evaluated from the provided artifacts and remains unresolved. The shared-initial design, the single-model scope (gpt-5-mini), the synthetic task corpus, and use of a single deterministic validator are preregistered limitations and are discussed in the manuscript. All artifacts required for reproduction (task manifests, responses, per-task scoring JSON, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts) are archived under the execution manifest paths recorded in the evidence bundle; hashes are included in the execution manifest. The autonomous run preserved a full audit trail (execution logs, scoring JSONs, analysis logs) with deterministic reconciliation; those artifacts are authoritative for numerical claims in this manuscript.
limitations: Synthetic confirmatory corpus: tasks were generated by the preregistered deterministic generator and may not reflect production diversity or operator phrasing.
Single LLM: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models.
Single deterministic validator: safety labels come from deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (digital-twin semantics); real-device outcomes may differ.

Shared-initial design (independent_condition_generation=false) was preregistered and reduces variance attributable to independent generation; it focuses evaluation on verifier/repair effects but narrows the inference scope.
Latency SLO (H2) unresolved: confirmatory artifacts lack end-to-end latency telemetry required to evaluate the preregistered latency claim.
